items.title: [MRV2] Cache multimodal prefix ranges per request
items.body:
## Purpose

`compute_mm_prefix_ranges` currently rebuilds PrefixLM multimodal document ranges on every MRV2 attention-preparation step, even though its current inputs are request-lifetime data for a request generation.

This change memoizes those per-request ranges in `EncoderCache` and reuses them across steps while still constructing a fresh batch-index dictionary for the current request order.

Implementation details:

- Keep the memo optional, so direct callers without it preserve existing behavior.
- Partition memoized ranges by `sliding_window`, the current semantic input that affects range filtering.
- Cache present requests, including present empty/non-visual requests, but do not accumulate absent request IDs.
- Let `EncoderCache` own the memo and invalidate a request across all memo contexts on add/replacement/remove.
- Do not mutate or clear previously returned lists during invalidation, so already-built metadata retains its original contents.
- Pass the memo from `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn` only under the existing multimodal PrefixLM gating.

Request finish/preemption and the existing remove/re-add path continue to provide the lifetime invalidation boundary. I also checked current MRV2 consumers of `mm_req_doc_ranges`; no in-place mutation of these range lists was found.

### Duplicate-work check

Before readiness I searched open vLLM PRs for `compute_mm_prefix_ranges` and for multimodal prefix-range caching. I found no existing request-lifetime cache for this host-side range construction.

The closest work is intentionally separate:

- #50539 changes V2 sliding-window/clamp semantics and proposes a new `clamp_in_kernel` semantic input to `compute_mm_prefix_ranges`; it does not cache per-request ranges.
- #48736 buckets downstream multimodal range widths to reduce Triton recompilations; it does not remove per-step host range extraction.

If #50539 lands first, this PR must be rebased so the memo context also includes its new semantic input rather than reusing ranges across different clamp modes.

## Test Plan

Focused correctness uses real `PlaceholderRange` / `MultiModalFeatureSpec` objects and CPU tensors. It covers range/mask semantics, sliding-window boundaries, absent/empty/non-visual requests, request reorder and fresh batch dictionaries, extract-once reuse, add/remove/replacement invalidation, same-object tensor mutation after remove/re-add, old-reference stability, multiple sliding-window contexts, and `DefaultModelState` wiring/gating.

I applied the same four-file patch cleanly onto upstream `main` at `ea723c81c3ea26425cb69503a5d5e90822a04a45` in a separate local checkout and ran the following with an existing vLLM-compatible virtualenv; no dependency installation or environment sync was performed:

```bash

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" <venv>/bin/python -m py_compile \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mm_prefix_ranges.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_cache.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/default.py
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" <venv>/bin/python -m ruff check \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mm_prefix_ranges.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py \
```

## Test Result

items.title: [Feature][KV Offload] Support joint GPU/CPU prefix cache lookup
items.body:
## Purpose

### Background

We deploy DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp with vLLM Ascend v0.27 in our internal network, with Simple CPU Offload enabled. During operation, we observed a cache miss rate exceeding 10%. Investigation showed that some reusable cache entries were not being retrieved due to the unimplemented TODO in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`: the existing API only matches a CPU suffix following the GPU prefix, rather than searching for a complete valid prefix across both pools.

After implementing joint lookup, we ported the change to the v0.27 branch in our fork and redeployed it in the same environment. The deployment has been running for five days, with normal operation and successful retrieval of cache entries previously affected by this limitation.

This PR targets upstream main. The deployment observations above come from the v0.27 backport in our fork.

### Changes

Support valid prefixes composed of interleaved GPU and CPU cache blocks, replacing the limitation of matching a GPU prefix followed by a CPU suffix.

For example, given a `GPU → CPU → GPU` cache layout, reuse both GPU blocks directly and allocate and load a target block only for the middle CPU block. When both pools contain a required block, prefer the GPU copy.

The implementation:

- Provides a read-only joint lookup view for existing attention-specific matching algorithms, preserving hybrid-attention convergence and memoizing queries within each request.
- Records hit sources by group and block position, distinguishing GPU hits, CPU blocks requiring loads, and attention padding.
- Pins source blocks before allocation and allocates targets only for CPU hits. Targets are registered in the cache after loading completes, without re-registering interleaved GPU hits.
- Attributes GPU/CPU cache statistics and cache events to their actual sources.
- Preserves full-block CPU loads, copy-on-write for partial GPU hits, and existing watermark and speculative-decoding reservation rules. If capacity is insufficient, allocation of the entire match is deferred.

### Relationship to related work

This PR implements joint lookup for interleaved GPU/CPU prefixes in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. The related #52773 / #52774 address boundary backfill in `OffloadingConnector`, so the connector and implementation scope differ.

## Test Plan

Cover the following behaviors:

- All-GPU, all-CPU, multiple interleavings, duplicate hits across pools, missing intermediate blocks, and different sources across groups.
- GPU block identity reuse, exact CPU transfer positions, and no publication of target cache entries before loading completes.
- SWA/Mamba, different block sizes, DCP/EAGLE matching boundaries, final-token recomputation, and copy-on-write for partial blocks.
- Insufficient capacity, speculative-decoding reservations, and reference cleanup after retries, cancellation, and reset.
- Bypassing separate GPU/CPU scans on the joint path, with no repeated probes for the same hash/group.
- GPU/CPU statistics and interleaved cache events.

Regression command after the latest code cleanup:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  -q
```

Run pre-commit on modified files, along with Python 3.10/3.12 type checks.

Local real-model validation uses OPT-125m, Qwen3-0.6B, and Qwen3.5-0.8B. GPU cache capacity is constrained and cache residency layouts are controlled to trigger actual CPU loads. Validation compares cold-cache and warm-cache outputs under deterministic generation settings and checks transfer positions and reference cleanup.

## Test Result

After the September 20 rebase, 575 distinct relevant tests passed (574 in the broad run and one rerun after restoring the Ray test dependency), along with pre-commit and Python 3.10/3.12 type checks. This includes regressions for discarding short joint hits under bounded prefix replay and replaying longer hits after CPU loading. Earlier, 22 real-model combinations passed, completing 9,146 exact cold/warm output comparisons and exercising actual CPU loads, copy-on-write, and preemption; that model matrix has not been rerun after this rebase. Some OPT/MTP combinations showed cold/warm differences that also reproduced on the legacy lookup path and are excluded from the passing results.

## AI assistance

GPT-6 Astra assisted with the implementation, tests, and this description. The code has undergone human review.

items.title: [Bugfix] Avoid O(n) strip_covered_mm_data work per realtime step
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58324.

Realtime (`/v1/realtime`) sessions re-enter the scheduler as new requests on every engine step. `NewRequestData.from_request` called `strip_covered_mm_data` over **all** accumulated multimodal features and `dataclasses.replace`'d every already-covered item. Per-step EngineCore time grew linearly with session age (~3 ms per minute of audio; quadratic over the session). A late-session profile put ~55% of EngineCore time in this path.

Covered features only grow, and `mm_features` are ordered by offset. This change:

1. Memoizes the stripped copy on each `MultiModalFeatureSpec`, so `dataclasses.replace` runs once per feature.
2. Keeps a covered prefix cache on `Request` (`_mm_stripped_prefix`) so later steps only examine newly covered features (O(new features), not O(all features)).

The scheduler-side `Request` still keeps the full payloads. Originals are not mutated. Preempt (`num_computed_tokens == 0`) clears the prefix cache so a later prefix-cache hit can re-strip from the originals.

**Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs for `#58324`, `strip_covered_mm_data`, and realtime scheduler mm-feature stripping. Issue #58324 is open with no linked PRs. `#52041` introduced the function; `#54994` only preserved SHM address items.

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. The submitting human reviewed the diff.

This does not change model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior — only scheduler CPU work for already-covered mm payloads.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_output.py -v --noconftest
```

CPU-only unit tests (no GPU). Existing `strip_covered_mm_data` cases plus reuse / O(new) / preempt-reset / `NewRequestData.from_request` identity checks.

## Test Result

```

======================== 10 passed, 1 warning in 3.55s =========================
```

All 10 tests passed, including:
- existing strip / mrope / SHM address cases
- memoized stripped-object identity (no extra `dataclasses.replace`)
- `stripped_prefix` cache is O(new features) on later steps
- preempt (`num_computed_tokens == 0`) resets the prefix cache
- `NewRequestData.from_request` reuses the request cache

items.title: [Core] Add waiting-queue-informed KV cache eviction
items.body:
## Purpose

Related to #48485.

When prefix caching is enabled, ordinary LRU eviction can discard blocks that
ready waiting requests are about to reuse. Those requests then recompute a
prefix even though evicting a different cached block would have kept the
allocation feasible.

This PR adds an allocator-local, best-effort eviction hint:

- the scheduler supplies a bounded, read-only snapshot of the ready `waiting`
  queue to each `allocate_slots()` transaction;
- `KVCacheManager` resolves matching block IDs lazily, memoizes them for that
  transaction, and clears the context in `finally`;
- `BlockPool` preserves existing LRU behavior unless an allocation would scan
  a cached candidate, then prefers non-retained free blocks while preserving
  order within the non-retained and retained groups;
- allocation, eviction, ref-count, metrics, and event ownership remain in the
  existing BlockPool path, and lookup/allocation exceptions still propagate.

The first slice intentionally excludes `skipped_waiting`, queue reordering,
block pinning/reservation, connector I/O, and new production metrics.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Focused eviction-hint behavior and scheduler wiring.
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k 'eviction_hint or popleft_n_with_hint or has_cached_block_in_first_n or block_pool_resolves_eviction_hint or block_pool_does_not_resolve_eviction_hint or allocate_slots_propagates_error_and_clears_hint_context or waiting_eviction_hint_resolver'

# Complete directly affected core suites.
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py

# Repository lint/format checks for all changed files.
python -m ruff check <changed-files>
python -m ruff format --check <changed-files>
```

The registered single-GPU integration plan uses Qwen3-0.6B, prefix caching,
priority scheduling, two running guard requests, an exact 320-block KV cache,
and five alternating fresh-server baseline/proposed pairs. It records exact
target-prefix evictions, cache-hit tokens, request-level TTFT/E2E latency,
preemptions, completed tokens/s, scheduler CPU time per step, GPU telemetry,
and paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

## Test Result

- Focused eviction-hint/context/provider/wiring tests: **14 passed**.
- Complete KV-cache utils, prefix-caching, and single-type-manager suites:
  **210 passed**.
- Ruff lint: **passed**; Ruff format check: **9 files already formatted**.
- `compileall` and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Five-pair Qwen3-0.6B A/B on one assigned RTX 4090: **BENEFICIAL**.
  Baseline evicted both target prefixes in 5/5 pairs; proposed evicted none and
  restored 192 cached tokens in 5/5 pairs. Mean scheduler CPU time was
  0.05790 ms/step baseline versus 0.06044 ms/step proposed (+4.38%, below the
  registered 5% ceiling). Target TTFT was effectively unchanged and its paired
  95% bootstrap CI crossed zero, so no latency improvement is claimed.

The local full scheduler file reached **120 passed** before its 36 multimodal
cases were blocked by a binary mismatch between the available precompiled
PyTorch and the current torchvision pin. The new scheduler wiring test itself
passes; the upstream CI matrix remains the authoritative multimodal check.

The worst-case selector microbenchmark (50,000 free blocks, 45,000 selected,
99% retained) measured 17.0 ms p95 for the hinted path versus 3.66 ms for plain
LRU. This is the deliberately pathological `O(F)` fallback bound; the paired
integration run above is used to quantify scheduler-step overhead in the
target workload.

For the paired run, both revisions used identical Qwen request warmups. The
public kernel configuration disabled optional JIT/CuTeDSL startup warmups and
FlashInfer autotune, and a benchmark-only shim skipped the unrelated
MiniMax-M3 multimodal warmup. These settings are benchmark-environment choices,
not changes in this PR.

items.title: [Rust Frontend] Avoid redundant decode per token in incremental detokenizer
items.body:
## Purpose

`DecodeStream::push_token` (the per-token streaming detokenization path) called
`tokenizer.decode()` twice per token: once to diff out the newly produced text,
and a second time only to recompute the `prefix` used as the next iteration's
byte offset. Since only `prefix.len()` is read downstream, and — for a
context-independent decoder — the retained tokens decode to exactly the suffix
already produced by the first decode, that second call is redundant. Reusing
the slice removes one of the two `decode()` calls per token.

This reuse is only sound when `decode(a ++ b) == decode(a) ++ decode(b)` at
token boundaries. That holds for byte-level decoders but not for
context-dependent ones such as Metaspace/SentencePiece, where a retained token
renders differently in isolation (e.g. a stripped leading space), which would
make `prefix.len()` wrong and silently swallow a token. So the fast path is
gated on a new `Tokenizer::decode_is_context_independent()` (default `false`);
context-dependent decoders keep the original re-decode behavior. The gate is
matched on the decoder itself — byte-level fastokens, and the HF backend when
its top-level decoder is `ByteLevel` — rather than on the backend enum.

## Test Plan

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-tokenizer
cargo bench -p vllm-tokenizer --bench hf -- tokenizer_incremental_decode
```

- `streaming_matches_full_decode_real_tokenizer`: streams a real byte-level BPE
  tokenizer (ASCII + CJK + emoji, so tokens routinely split multi-byte
  characters across boundaries) and asserts the incremental output is
  byte-identical to a full `decode()`.
- `streaming_matches_full_decode_metaspace`: a Metaspace tokenizer stays on the
  re-decode path and streams correctly (the leading-space case the fast path
  would break).
- `adversarial_byte_streams_match_full_decode`: streams byte sequences with
  invalid UTF-8 at and across token boundaries (lone lead bytes, stray
  continuations, permanently invalid bytes, literal U+FFFD output, dangling
  lead byte at flush) and asserts streamed output equals a one-shot decode.
- `tokenizer_incremental_decode` benchmarks both the fastokens byte-level and HF
  backends (the path had no benchmark before this PR).

## Test Result

- 44 tests pass; `clippy -D warnings` and `rustfmt --check` clean.
- Criterion (Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B tokenizer, ~2.8k-token stream, isolated target
  dir per variant, alternated runs):

  | `tokenizer_incremental_decode` | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `fastokens` (byte-level; default loader path) | 425–457 µs | ~334 µs (**~21–26%**) |
  | `hf_tokenizers` (fallback backend) | ~1.18 ms | ~745 µs (**~37%**) |

---

AI assistance was used to investigate and implement this change. I have reviewed
and verified every changed line, the correctness tests, and the benchmark
results.

items.title: [Perf][Frontend] Add opt-in incremental prompt-encoding cache for multi-turn chat
items.body:
RFC: #47582


## Purpose

In multi-turn chat, every request re-sends the whole conversation, so the rendered prompt of turn `N` is almost always a strict string prefix of turn `N+1` — yet `BaseRenderer._tokenize_prompt` re-tokenizes the full prompt every turn. That cost is linear in history length (~0.5 s per turn at ~200K tokens) and lands on the API-server CPU, where it competes with detokenization and chat-template rendering (#39590). With automatic prefix caching, tokenization is frequently the dominant TTFT term for long conversations.

This PR adds an **opt-in**, token-exact incremental encoding cache:

- `--enable-incremental-encoding` engine/CLI flag (default **off**), env fallback `VLLM_INCREMENTAL_ENCODING=1`.
- Related but different from segment-parallel/segment-cache tokenization (#45514), which accelerates cold large prompts; this reuses the *previous request's* encoding across the multi-turn sequence. The two compose. SGLang's SMG L1 prefix tokenization cache is ecosystem precedent.

Production validation: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2×DGX-Spark (agentic coding, long conversations) — median multi-turn TTFT **0.92 s → 0.47 s**, encode ~35× faster at the median, token-exact on all sampled turns.

## How it works

`vllm/tokenizers/incremental_encode.py` (dependency-free, ~450 lines incl. docs):

1. Bounded LRU (16 entries) of recent `(text, token_ids)` pairs, longest-prefix match, optional `cache_salt` partitioning (the OpenAI frontend is stateless).
2. On a prefix hit, back up a 1024-char window from the cached text's end and take pre-token boundary candidates ≥96 chars from either window edge via the fast backend's `pre_tokenizer.pre_tokenize_str`. **BPE merges never cross pre-token boundaries**, so tokens strictly before such a boundary don't depend on appended text.
3. The seam must have no `<|` marker within ±96 chars and must coincide with a token boundary in the cached encoding's char offsets (rules out seams inside added/special tokens).
4. Re-encode only from the seam; **verify** the overlap token ids + offsets against the cached encoding (excluding the last 96 chars, which may merge with new text); splice `cached_prefix_ids + tail_ids`.
5. Everything unprovable falls back to a full encode (and refreshes the cache): no usable boundary, normalizer rewrites the window, verification mismatch, non-template special-token semantics (probed per `add_special_tokens` value), results exceeding `truncation`/`max_length` (returned to the regular path so truncation-side semantics stay untouched), prompts < 16K chars.

Wiring is minimal: `BaseRenderer._tokenize_prompt` consults the cache first and falls through to the existing `tokenizer(...)` call whenever the cache returns `None`. The cache sits **above** the deep-copied tokenizer pool (`maybe_make_thread_pool`) and is thread-safe; the lock covers only lookup/insert. Scope is HF fast tokenizers only — mistral/deepseek_v32/harmony renderers are untouched and the flag is silently inert for them. Default behavior is completely unchanged (`enable_incremental_encoding=False`).

Non-test footprint: 490 added lines (446 module incl. docstrings + 44 wiring/config/env).

## Benchmarks

`benchmarks/benchmark_incremental_encoding.py` (transformers-only; measures per-turn encode latency for growing synthetic conversations, asserting token-exactness every turn).

This machine (Python 3.14, tokenizers 0.22.2, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B` tokenizer, 8 turns/size):

| history (tokens) | cold p50 | cold p99 | incr p50 | incr p99 | speedup (p50) | hit/miss/fallback |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5,000 | 3.97 ms | 4.19 ms | 0.69 ms | 0.70 ms | 5.8× | 8/1/0 |
| 32,000 | 25.67 ms | 26.03 ms | 1.17 ms | 1.25 ms | 22.0× | 8/1/0 |
| 128,000 | 151.82 ms | 155.23 ms | 2.77 ms | 2.89 ms | 54.9× | 8/1/0 |
| 512,000 | 782.94 ms | 786.05 ms | 10.95 ms | 12.06 ms | 71.5× | 8/1/0 |

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` tokenizer: 32K → 35.66 ms vs 1.45 ms (24.6×); 128K → 160.40 ms vs 3.12 ms (51.4×).

Production (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 2×DGX-Spark): median multi-turn TTFT 0.92 s → 0.47 s.

## Test Plan

`tests/tokenizers_/test_incremental_encode.py` — pure unit tests against real HF tokenizers, no GPU/engine required (the module is dependency-free, so they also run in a bare transformers venv):

- Growing 8-turn conversations with adversarial content (code, CJK/Korean/Japanese, emoji ZWJ sequences, RTL, combining marks, whitespace runs, literal `<|im_start|>`/`<|endoftext|>`/`<|begin▁of▁sentence|>` strings) asserted **token-exact vs full re-encode at every turn**, for `add_special_tokens` True and False, across `openai-community/gpt2`, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` — with assertions that the splice path (not just fallback) is exercised.
- Interleaved concurrent conversations sharing the LRU; identical-prompt memoization; appends starting at/after special tokens; whitespace runs spanning the seam.
- Guard rails: kwargs compatibility rejection, truncation-overflow fallback, `cache_salt` partitioning, LRU bound, non-fast tokenizer rejection, short-prompt gate.

## Test Result

- 37/37 passed (12 test cases × 3 tokenizers + 1 tokenizer-independent): gpt2 12/12, Qwen2.5-0.5B 12/12, DeepSeek-V3 12/12, non-fast gate 1/1.
- Additional concurrency check: 8 threads × 6-turn conversations against a pool-wrapped (deep-copy pool, as in `maybe_make_thread_pool`) tokenizer — 40 hits / 8 misses / 0 fallbacks, all token-exact.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean on all touched files.

## Notes

- DCO: all commits are signed off (`git commit -s`).
- An accompanying RFC issue covers motivation, alternatives (including doing this in the Rust frontend — the algorithm is self-contained and ports; the Python path remains the default today), and the relationship to #45514.

items.title: [Bugfix] Encode special tokens found in text for MistralCommonBackend in multimodal processors
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #50706

vLLM crashes at engine startup for Mistral3/Pixtral models whose tokenizer resolves to transformers' `MistralCommonBackend`. Per transformers' `AutoTokenizer` resolution, this happens whenever `mistral-common` is installed (`is_mistral_common_available()`) and the model's `model_type` (`mistral`/`ministral`/`mistral3`/etc) is mapped to `MistralCommonBackend` in `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` — whether or not the checkpoint ships more than one tokenizer format plays no part (h/t @hmellor for the correction). Affected checkpoints include e.g. `nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4`, `mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B`. `MistralCommonBackend` never encodes special tokens (e.g. `"[IMG]"`) found in plain text.

During dummy multimodal input profiling (run at engine startup to size the encoder budget), `PixtralProcessor` counts a mismatch between the placeholder in the templated text and the encoded ids and raises:

```
ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1].
ValueError: Failed to apply PixtralProcessor on data={'text': '[IMG]'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'}
```

`InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` now swaps in a `MistralCommonBackend` subclass (`with_placeholder_token_support`) that resolves known special-token strings found in text back to their ids, scoped only to the tokenizer instance handed to HF processors — never used for general/user-prompt tokenization.

Conceptually related to but independently derived from:
- #50752 — fixes the same root cause on the default tokenizer-mode path (currently blocked on the contributor-gate CI check, not real test failures)
- #45525 — fixes the sibling issue (#45289) for `--tokenizer-mode mistral`

## Test Plan

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This pull request optimizes Gemma 4 multimodal processing in `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` and adds comprehensive unit tests in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_mm_optimizations.py`. It accelerates vision/audio preprocessing, projection, and multimodal serving across all 5 Gemma 4 model architectures (`google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, `google/gemma-4-12B-it`, `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, and `google/gemma-4-31B-it`):

1. **Batched Vision Spatial Pooling (`Gemma4VisionPooler`)**: Replaces the sequential per-image and per-frame Python loops over `vt.pooler(...)` with resolution-grouped batched pooling and standardization, plus an identity-pooling mask guard (`pooling_kernel_size == 1`), delivering up to **27.60x** speedup on multi-frame video pooling (**100.0% bit-exact**).
2. **Fused Vision/Audio RMSNorm via `vllm_c` (`Gemma4VisionRMSNorm`)**: Replaces eager HuggingFace `Gemma4RMSNorm` modules across the vision and audio towers with `Gemma4VisionRMSNorm(RMSNorm)` (credit to `@cjackal`), dispatching directly to `ir.ops.rms_norm.impls["vllm_c"]` (`csrc/layernorm_kernels.cu`) for both scaled (`with_scale=True`) and unscaled (`with_scale=False`) RMSNorm while preserving loaded parameter references and safe fallback guards. Delivers **2.83x - 9.40x** speedup (**100.0% bit-exact / 1-ULP**).
3. **Fused 2D Rotary Position Embeddings (`fused_vision_2d_rope`)**: Fuses 4-quarter axial 2D rotary position embeddings into a single Triton kernel (`_vision_2d_rope_kernel`, tuned with `num_warps=2`, broadcast stride handling, and empty-tensor guards). Delivers **3.21x - 6.83x** speedup (**96.3% - 96.4% within 1-ULP**, cosine similarity **0.999998**).
4. **O(1) Full-Attention Layer Prefix Mask Clearing**: Replaces per-step string splitting of attention layer names with precomputed frozen set indices (`self._full_attn_layer_idxs`) and bounded memoized lookup (`self._cached_full_attn_layer_names`), reducing bidirectional attention prefix clearing overhead by **3.12x - 3.29x** (**100.0% bit-exact**).

Duplicate-work check: verified via `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "Gemma 4 vision pooler 2D RoPE"` and `gh issue list` that no open pull request addresses vision pooler batching or 2D RoPE fusion for Gemma 4.

## Claims

- **Realistic End-to-End V1 Serving Speedup (`enforce_eager=False`, `torch.compile` + CUDAGraphs)**:
  - On `gemma-4-E2B-it`: delivers **1.25x - 1.35x** speedup on single-image prefill, **1.13x - 1.28x** speedup on 4-image multi-modal prefill, and **1.16x - 1.25x** speedup on steady-state multimodal serving across batch sizes 1 to 8.
  - On `gemma-4-E4B-it`: delivers **1.13x - 1.22x** speedup on single-image prefill, **1.17x - 1.29x** speedup on 4-image multi-modal prefill, and **1.06x - 1.13x** speedup on steady-state multimodal serving across batch sizes 1 to 8.
  - On `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (MoE): delivers **1.25x - 1.33x** speedup on single-image prefill, **1.26x - 1.27x** speedup on 4-image multi-modal prefill, and **1.11x - 1.19x** speedup on steady-state multimodal serving across batch sizes 1 to 8.
  - On `gemma-4-31B-it` (Dense): delivers **1.14x - 1.16x** speedup on single-image prefill, **1.15x** speedup on 4-image multi-modal prefill, and **1.04x - 1.07x** speedup on steady-state multimodal serving across batch sizes 1 to 4.
  - Unique `multi_modal_uuids` were supplied on every iteration to guarantee full end-to-end execution through the encoder, pooler, projector, and language backbone without caching shortcuts.
- **Multimodal Tower Pipeline Speedup (SigLIP Tower + Batched Pooler + Projection)**:
  - `gemma-4-E2B-it`: **1.63x - 1.85x** speedup across single/multi-image and video frame configurations.
  - `gemma-4-E4B-it`: **1.66x - 2.29x** speedup across single/multi-image and video frame configurations.
  - `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`: **1.67x - 2.14x** speedup across single/multi-image and video frame configurations.

  - `Gemma4RMSNorm with_scale=True Vision` (B=1..16, L=900, D=1152): **3.33x - 9.40x** speedup (+233.3% to +840.4% gain).
  - `Gemma4RMSNorm with_scale=True Audio` (B=1..16, L=900, D=1024): **3.58x - 8.63x** speedup (+258.1% to +762.8% gain).

- **Unified Architecture Regression Parity**:

```python
def compute_parity_metrics(base: Any, feat: Any) -> Dict[str, float]:
    if isinstance(base, (tuple, list)):
        metrics_list = [compute_parity_metrics(b, f) for b, f in zip(base, feat)]
        return {
            "bit_exact_pct": float(sum(m["bit_exact_pct"] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)),
            "within_1ulp_pct": float(sum(m["within_1ulp_pct"] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)),
            "max_abs_diff": float(max(m["max_abs_diff"] for m in metrics_list)),
            "cosine_sim": float(min(m["cosine_sim"] for m in metrics_list)),
        }
    if isinstance(base, dict):
        metrics_list = [compute_parity_metrics(base[k], feat[k]) for k in base]
        return {
            "bit_exact_pct": float(sum(m["bit_exact_pct"] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)),
            "within_1ulp_pct": float(sum(m["within_1ulp_pct"] for m in metrics_list) / len(metrics_list)),
            "max_abs_diff": float(max(m["max_abs_diff"] for m in metrics_list)),
            "cosine_sim": float(min(m["cosine_sim"] for m in metrics_list)),
        }

    assert isinstance(base, torch.Tensor) and isinstance(feat, torch.Tensor)
    base_cpu, feat_cpu = base.detach().cpu(), feat.detach().cpu()
    total_elems = base_cpu.numel()
    if total_elems == 0:
        return {"bit_exact_pct": 100.0, "within_1ulp_pct": 100.0, "max_abs_diff": 0.0, "cosine_sim": 1.0}

    elem_exact = (base_cpu.contiguous().view(torch.uint8) == feat_cpu.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)).all(dim=-1)
    bit_exact_pct = float(elem_exact.float().mean().item() * 100.0)

    base_f, feat_f = base_cpu.float(), feat_cpu.float()
    diff = (base_f - feat_f).abs()
    max_abs_diff = float(diff.max().item()) if diff.numel() > 0 else 0.0

    if base_cpu.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
        a_i, b_i = base_cpu.view(torch.int16), feat_cpu.view(torch.int16)
        same_sign = (a_i >= 0) == (b_i >= 0)
        ulp = torch.where(same_sign, (a_i.int() - b_i.int()).abs(), torch.tensor(999999, device=base_cpu.device))
        ulp = torch.where((a_i == b_i) | ((base_cpu == 0) & (feat_cpu == 0)) | (diff <= 1e-6), 0, ulp)
        within_1ulp = ulp <= 1
    else:
        within_1ulp = diff <= 1e-4
    within_1ulp_pct = float(within_1ulp.float().mean().item() * 100.0)

    if total_elems > 1:
        base_d, feat_d = base_f.flatten().double(), feat_f.flatten().double()
        norm_b, norm_f = torch.linalg.norm(base_d), torch.linalg.norm(feat_d)
        if norm_b == 0 or norm_f == 0:
            cos_sim = 1.0 if norm_b == norm_f else 0.0
        else:
            denom = torch.clamp(norm_b * norm_f, min=1e-12)
            cos_sim = float(torch.clamp((base_d * feat_d).sum() / denom, -1.0, 1.0).item())
    else:
        cos_sim = 1.0 if max_abs_diff == 0.0 else 0.0

    return {
        "bit_exact_pct": bit_exact_pct,
        "within_1ulp_pct": within_1ulp_pct,
        "max_abs_diff": max_abs_diff,
        "cosine_sim": cos_sim,
    }


def measure_cuda_latency(fn: Callable[[], Any], warmup: int = 5, reps: int = 20) -> float:
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    start_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(reps)]
    end_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(reps)]

    for i in range(reps):
        start_events[i].record()
        fn()
        end_events[i].record()

    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times = sorted([s.elapsed_time(e) for s, e in zip(start_events, end_events)])
    return float(times[len(times) // 2])

            # Build inputs with unique UUIDs to bypass multimodal encoder cache on every call
            def make_inputs():
```

items.title: [Tokenizer] Add batch_split_message tokenizer mode for lossless segmented encoding
items.body:
## Motivation

In multi-turn / long-conversation serving, the tokenization stage takes a non-trivial slice of TTFT: the prompt grows long, the HF fast tokenizer encodes a single long sequence on one thread, and tokenization cost grows linearly with prompt length. This PR introduces a lossless segmented parallel-encoding scheme, plus a cache for long, highly-reusable segments, substantially cutting the tokenization latency in multi-turn / long-sequence serving.

`batch_split_message` cuts tokenization latency in two independent ways:

- **Parallelism:** split the text on a special-token delimiter (default: eos) and encode the segments in a single `encode_batch`, which the underlying Rust tokenizer parallelizes across segments — so the tokenization cost drops from encoding the whole prompt to encoding the longest single segment.
- **Segment reuse (optional cache):** in many deployments the system prompt and tool definitions are a large, fixed share of the prompt and are fully reusable across requests, while the user message is far smaller than these segments. With those long segments cached, the tokenizer only needs to encode the user segment.

It is lossless: when the delimiter is a registered special token (a hard BPE boundary), the produced token ids are byte-for-byte identical to a single `encode()`.

## What it does

- `encode(text)` → split on delimiter → `encode_batch(segments)` (parallel) → concat with the delimiter ids in between.
- **Lossless guard:** for tokenizers that inject specials on encode (`num_special_tokens_to_add() > 0`), the completion path (`add_special_tokens=True`) falls back to a single `encode` so BOS/EOS isn't repeated per segment. The chat path (`add_special_tokens=False`) always segments. Tokenizers that add nothing (e.g. Qwen/ChatML) segment in both paths.
- **Optional `segment_cache`:** a thread-safe LRU (keyed by a content digest, bounded by both entry count and total tokens) memoizing segment→token-ids. It lives at the tokenizer layer and is orthogonal to the KV prefix cache — it saves re-tokenization regardless of whether the prefix cache hits.
- Follows the existing `get_cached_tokenizer` pattern — a dynamic subclass swaps `__class__` and only `encode` is overridden, so every other `TokenizerLike` method is inherited unchanged. Registered in both the tokenizer and renderer registries (the renderer reuses `HfRenderer`).

## Design / API note (feedback welcome)

Configuration is passed through a new `--tokenizer-mode-config` (a dict, `ModelConfig.tokenizer_mode_config`), forwarded to the tokenizer's `from_pretrained`:

```
--tokenizer-mode batch_split_message \
--tokenizer-mode-config '{"segment_cache": true, "cache_max_entries": 100000}'
```

Keys (all optional): `split_delimiter` (default: eos), `segment_cache` (default: false), `cache_max_entries` (default: 100000), `cache_max_tokens` (default: 8000000).

This adds a general config entry for custom tokenizer modes. Alternatives considered: reusing `hf_overrides` (rejected — it targets the HF *config*, different semantics) or a mode-specific flag (rejected — pollutes the global args and doesn't generalize). Happy to adjust the name/shape if a more constrained or differently-named entry is preferred.

## Changes

- `vllm/tokenizers/batch_split_message.py` (new): core implementation + `_SegmentIdsCache`.
- `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py`, `vllm/renderers/registry.py`: register the mode (renderer reuses `HfRenderer`).
- `vllm/config/model.py`: `TokenizerMode` literal + `tokenizer_mode_config` field.
- `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`: expose `--tokenizer-mode-config`.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_batch_split_message.py`, `benchmarks/benchmark_batch_split_tokenizer.py` (new).

Default behavior is unchanged: the mode is opt-in and the cache is off by default.

## Tests

`tests/tokenizers_/test_batch_split_message.py` (small Qwen tokenizer): lossless equivalence vs a single `encode` across edge cases (empty, leading/trailing/ consecutive delimiters, multi-turn), `add_special_tokens=False` equivalence, completion-path fallback, truncation, segment-cache hit/eviction (entry + token bounds, oversized rejection), and concurrent-encode consistency.

## Performance

Standalone tokenizer benchmark (`benchmarks/benchmark_batch_split_tokenizer.py`) — measures the tokenizer only (no engine, no GPU).

**Setup**
- Host: 31-core CPU.
- Tokenizer: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8; delimiter `<|im_end|>` (eos); `add_special_tokens=False` (chat path).
- Prompt sizes (`total`): 5000 / 10000 / 30000 / 50000 / 100000 / 150000 / 200000 tokens, capped at the model's max sequence length.
- Segments per prompt (`segs`): 5 for `total <= 30000`, else 10. Per-segment lengths are jittered (longest/shortest ratio ~= 3) and sum to `total`.
- Cache hit rate (`reuse`): 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 — each segment reuses an already-seen segment with this probability.
- 10 warmup + 100 measured encodes per cell; report p50 and p99.

**Configs compared (identical prompts across all three)**
- `plain` — normal HF tokenizer (`tokenizer_mode=hf`).
- `seg` — `batch_split_message`, segment cache **off** (parallelism only).
- `cache` — `batch_split_message`, segment cache **on**.

**Column meanings**
- `total` — target prompt size (tokens); `real_tok` — actual encoded length (median; differs slightly because random-token text re-encodes non-identically).
- `segs` — segments per prompt; `reuse` — configured reuse probability; `hit%` — measured **segment-level** hit rate (cached segments / total segments). The cache is keyed per segment: when a whole segment is already cached, its token ids are returned directly and re-encoding is skipped.
- `plain(ms)` / `seg(ms)` / `cache(ms)` — per-encode latency of each config.
- `seg/plain` — parallel speedup = `plain / seg` (×, higher is faster).
- `cache/seg` — incremental cache speedup = `seg / cache` (×).

items.body:
## Overview

This pull request enables and optimizes KV-sharing fast prefill (You Only Cache Once / YOCO architecture) in vLLM V1 across attention utilities, worker runtime, and model configuration:

1. **Auto-Enablement of Fast Prefill**: In `vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`, automatically initializes `kv_sharing_fast_prefill = True` in `Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config` when KV-shared layers are detected (`num_kv_shared_layers > 0`), speculative decoding is inactive (`speculative_config is None`), pipeline parallelism is unitary (`pipeline_parallel_size == 1`), and non-diffusion (`DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion not in architectures`). This ensures out-of-the-box acceleration for `gemma-4-E2B-it` and `gemma-4-E4B-it` without requiring explicit CLI flags.
2. **Piecewise CUDAGraph Integration & Compiled Cross-Decoder Norm**: In `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py`, moves `self.norm` into `Gemma4CrossDecoderLayers` (matching how `Gemma4SelfDecoderLayers` holds `embed_tokens` and `per_layer_projection_norm`) so `torch.compile` and `CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE` fuse and capture `self.norm` directly inside the compiled `cross_decoder` subgraph rather than executing eagerly outside `torch.compile`. Removes redundant `positions` buffer copy before `self.self_decoder`, equips `Gemma4Model.fast_prefill_forward` with piecewise CUDAGraph dispatch for cross-decoder execution, pre-allocated static tensor buffers, zero-copy decode fast-path, and sliced assignment `self_decoder_hidden_states[logits_indices_padded[:num_logits_indices]] = cross_hidden_states[:num_logits_indices]` to ensure padding tokens are never copied.
3. **Analytical Range Construction for Single-Logit Requests**: In `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py`, when `common_attn_metadata.max_logits_per_req == 1 and num_logits_indices == num_reqs`, by the pigeonhole principle every request in the batch samples strictly 1 token, guaranteeing that `decode_query_start_loc` is identical to `[0, 1, 2, ..., num_reqs]`. Constructing `decode_query_start_loc` directly via `torch.arange` on GPU and CPU replaces 6 GPU kernel launches (`torch.bucketize`, `torch.zeros`, `torch.ones_like`, `scatter_add_`, `fill_`, `torch.cumsum`) and 1 PCIe D2H transfer with 1 GPU `torch.arange` kernel (net reduction of 5 GPU kernel launches and 1 PCIe D2H copy).
4. **Pure-Decode Step Preparation Guard**: In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, guards `_prepare_kv_sharing_fast_prefill(logits_indices)` with `and max_query_len > 1`, completely skipping redundant GPU buffer copy/fill (`kv_sharing_fast_prefill_logits_indices`) and CUDAGraph dispatch on pure-decode steps (`max_query_len == 1`).
5. **Metadata Class and Custom Backend Factory Memoization (`@functools.lru_cache`)**: In `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py`, dynamic creation of `class KVSharingFastPrefillAttentionMetadata(metadata_cls, KVSharingFastPrefillMetadata)` inside `FastPrefillAttentionBuilder.build()` invoked `typing._ProtocolMeta.__new__` (`ABCMeta.__new__`) and `dataclasses.fields()` on every forward step. Added `_get_fast_prefill_metadata_cls(metadata_cls: type)` cached via `@functools.lru_cache`, creating the wrapper class once per underlying metadata class. Decorated `create_fast_prefill_custom_backend` with `@functools.lru_cache` so identical `(prefix, underlying_attn_backend)` pairs reuse the same `AttentionBackend` and `FastPrefillAttentionBuilder` classes across layers and KV-cache groups.
6. **Pure-Decode Step Same-Group Attention Metadata Reuse**: In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`, within each KV cache group (`kv_cache_gid`), donor layers (`attn_gid=0`) and recipient layers (`attn_gid=1`) share the exact same `KVCacheSpec`. On pure-decode steps (`logits_indices_padded is None` and `not for_cudagraph_capture`), both builders produce identical attention metadata for the same `(kv_cache_gid, kv_cache_spec, cascade_attn_prefix_len)`. Introduced `same_group_decode_cache` in `_build_attention_metadata`, allowing recipient attention groups to directly reuse the already-built `attn_metadata_i` without invoking `builder.build(...)` a second time.

Duplicate-work check: verified via `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "KV-sharing fast prefill"` and `gh issue list` that no open pull request addresses KV-sharing fast prefill auto-enablement, piecewise CUDAGraph execution, or single-logit metadata specialization in V1.

## Claims

- **End-to-End Out-of-the-Box Serving Speedup (`enforce_eager=False`, torch.compile + CUDAGraphs)**:
  - On `gemma-4-E2B-it`: delivers **1.34x - 2.06x** speedup on prefill-heavy workloads (up to **+106.0% throughput gain**, latency drops from 416.45 ms to 202.28 ms at BS16), **1.01x - 1.75x** speedup on balanced workloads (up to **+75.0% throughput gain**, latency drops from 229.28 ms to 131.18 ms at BS16), **1.04x - 1.21x** speedup on decode-heavy workloads at BS8-BS16 (up to **+21.0% throughput gain** at BS16), and **1.95x - 2.10x** speedup on long-context 4K prefill workloads (up to **+110.0% throughput gain**, latency drops from 500.73 ms to 238.37 ms at BS4).
  - On `gemma-4-E4B-it`: delivers **1.41x - 1.54x** speedup on prefill-heavy workloads (up to **+54.1% throughput gain**, latency drops from 685.48 ms to 444.75 ms at BS16), **1.11x - 1.45x** speedup on balanced workloads (up to **+45.3% throughput gain**, latency drops from 367.97 ms to 253.29 ms at BS16), **1.02x - 1.20x** speedup on decode-heavy workloads at BS4-BS16 (up to **+19.9% throughput gain** at BS16), and **1.52x - 1.57x** speedup on long-context 4K prefill workloads (up to **+56.7% throughput gain**, latency drops from 767.06 ms to 489.57 ms at BS4).

## Details

### Root Cause
In models using KV-sharing architectures (such as Gemma 4 E2B/E4B), non-shared layers execute full attention across all sequence tokens, whereas shared layers only compute attention for newly sampled prompt tokens (fast prefill). In upstream `main` (`b6d8e8afd9`), fast prefill was disabled by default (`kv_sharing_fast_prefill = False`), leaving users with full prefill computation across all shared layers and forfeiting massive throughput improvements.

Furthermore:
1. `make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata` unconditionally ran a generalized scatter/histogram pipeline to compute per-request decode token counts:
   - `torch.bucketize` to map logit indices to request IDs.
   - `torch.zeros` and `torch.ones_like` tensor allocations.
   - `scatter_add_` to count decode tokens per request.
   - `torch.empty`, `fill_(0)`, and `torch.cumsum` to construct `decode_query_start_loc`.
   - Non-blocking D2H transfer `decode_query_start_loc.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` to populate `decode_query_start_loc_cpu`.
   While avoiding host-blocking synchronizations, executing 6 GPU kernel launches and a PCIe transfer introduces fixed kernel launch overhead per prefill request. For single-logit sampling (`max_logits_per_req == 1`), every request contributes exactly 1 token, making dynamic histogram computation redundant.
2. On pure-decode steps (`max_query_len == 1`), `GPUModelRunner._build_attention_metadata` did not guard `_prepare_kv_sharing_fast_prefill(logits_indices)`, unconditionally executing GPU buffer copy and fill over 8192 tokens (`kv_sharing_fast_prefill_logits_indices`) even though `make_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_common_attn_metadata` immediately returns when `max_query_len == 1`.
3. In `Gemma4Model`, `self.norm` was applied eagerly outside `torch.compile` after `cross_decoder` on every step, rather than being captured inside `Gemma4CrossDecoderLayers` alongside the decoder layers, and redundant buffer copy of `positions` occurred before `self_decoder`.

### Design & Implementation
1. **Config Auto-Enablement in `config.py`**: When `num_kv_shared_layers > 0`, `speculative_config is None`, `parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size == 1`, and `DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion not in architectures`, `Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config` automatically sets `kv_sharing_fast_prefill = True` in `CacheConfig`, enabling fast prefill by default for all KV-sharing models while preserving explicit user overrides.
2. **Piecewise CUDAGraph & Model Optimizations in `gemma4.py`**:
   - Moved `self.norm` into `Gemma4CrossDecoderLayers` so `torch.compile` and `CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE` fuse and capture `self.norm` inside the compiled `cross_decoder` subgraph, returning normalized hidden states directly without eager post-processing.
   - Removed redundant `self.positions[:batch_size].copy_(positions)` before `self.self_decoder`.
   - Integrated piecewise CUDAGraph dispatch for the cross-decoder when `self._use_piecewise_cudagraph and num_padded in self._cudagraph_capture_sizes and (orig_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE or compilation_counter.num_cudagraph_captured > 0)`. This allows cross-decoder piecewise CUDAGraph replay on prefill batches even when `total_tokens > 512` (`orig_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.NONE`), while avoiding default stream capture errors during `_warmup_kernels` (`num_cudagraph_captured == 0`).
   - Removed `.clone()` in `fast_prefill_forward`, directly indexing into pre-allocated static GPU buffers (`self.positions`, `self.hidden_states`, `self.per_layer_inputs`).
   - Added a dedicated decode fast path when `logits_indices_padded is None` to bypass index lookup operations.
   - Sliced assignment: `self_decoder_hidden_states[logits_indices_padded[:num_logits_indices]] = cross_hidden_states[:num_logits_indices]`, ensuring padding tokens are never copied.
3. **Pigeonhole Specialization in `utils.py`**: When `common_attn_metadata.max_logits_per_req == 1 and num_logits_indices == num_reqs`, each request samples strictly 1 token. Therefore, `decode_query_start_loc` is guaranteed to be `[0, 1, ..., num_reqs]`. We directly construct `torch.arange(0, num_reqs + 1, device=device, dtype=query_start_loc.dtype)` on GPU and `torch.arange(0, num_reqs + 1, device="cpu", dtype=query_start_loc.dtype)` on CPU. This replaces 6 GPU kernel launches (`torch.bucketize`, `torch.zeros`, `torch.ones_like`, `scatter_add_`, `fill_`, `torch.cumsum`) and 1 PCIe D2H transfer with 1 GPU `torch.arange` kernel.
4. **Pure-Decode Guard in `gpu_model_runner.py`**: Added `and max_query_len > 1` to the KV-sharing condition in `GPUModelRunner._build_attention_metadata`. On pure-decode steps (`max_query_len == 1`), buffer staging and CUDAGraph dispatch are bypassed, saving ~0.04 ms per decode step and aligning V1 `GPUModelRunner` with V2 `FastPrefillHelper.prepare`.
5. **Metadata Class Memoization & Factory Caching in `utils.py`**:
   - `_get_fast_prefill_metadata_cls(metadata_cls: type)`: Decorating this class factory with `@functools.lru_cache` eliminates dynamic creation of `class KVSharingFastPrefillAttentionMetadata(metadata_cls, KVSharingFastPrefillMetadata)` and `typing._ProtocolMeta.__new__` / `dataclasses.fields()` on every forward step, constructing the wrapper class once per unique metadata type.
   - `create_fast_prefill_custom_backend`: Decorating with `@functools.lru_cache` ensures identical `(prefix, underlying_attn_backend)` pairs reuse the same custom backend and builder classes across layers and KV-cache groups.
6. **Pure-Decode Same-Group Attention Metadata Reuse in `gpu_model_runner.py`**:
   - On pure-decode steps (`logits_indices_padded is None` and `not for_cudagraph_capture`) with `kv_sharing_fast_prefill=True`, donor layers (`attn_gid=0`) and recipient layers (`attn_gid=1`) within each KV-cache group share the exact same `KVCacheSpec` and `cascade_attn_prefix_len`.
   - `same_group_decode_cache: dict[tuple[int, KVCacheSpec, int], AttentionMetadata]` captures the built metadata from `attn_gid=0` and directly serves `attn_gid=1`, eliminating duplicate `builder.build(...)` execution on pure-decode steps.
7. **Speculative Decoding Fallback**: When `max_logits_per_req > 1` (e.g. speculative decoding draft tokens), execution falls back to the generalized `scatter_add_` + `cumsum` path, guaranteeing 100.0% numerical compatibility and zero regression.

items.title: refactor(envs): migrate vllm/envs.py to pydantic-settings
items.body:
## Summary

Refactors `vllm/envs.py` to use `pydantic-settings`, addressing [RFC #31249](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31249).

Each env var now has a **single declaration** — type, default, description, and (where relevant) alias or validator — on a domain-specific `BaseSettings` sub-class. The public `vllm.envs.VLLM_X` attribute API is preserved. Anything derived from env vars (the docs page, `torch.compile` cache keys) is generated from those field declarations instead of hand-maintained parallel lists, so it cannot drift.

## Architecture

- Env vars are grouped into domain-specific `BaseSettings` sub-classes (build, paths, server, logging, distributed, compilation, media, CPU, ROCm, TPU/XPU, FlashInfer, quant, connector, usage), composed into one root `Settings`.
- `env_prefix="VLLM_"` covers the majority of fields. Non-`VLLM_` vars (`MAX_JOBS`, `S3_*`, `LOCAL_RANK`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `NO_COLOR`, …) use explicit `alias=`.
- Cross-cutting defaults (e.g. `VLLM_DP_RANK_LOCAL` → `VLLM_DP_RANK`, torch-version-dependent AOT flags, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` ↔ `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_LOCATION`) live in a root `@model_validator(mode="after")`. `VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK` / `DO_NOT_TRACK` fallback uses `AliasChoices`.
- Hand-rolled coercion helpers (`maybe_convert_int`, `env_with_choices`, `env_list_with_choices`, `get_env_or_set_default`, `use_aot_compile`, …) are deleted in favor of pydantic's native parsing, `Literal`, and validators.
- `environment_variables` and `maybe_convert_bool` are kept as back-compat shims for external callers (`vllm/collect_env.py`, `vllm/ray/ray_env.py`, `tests/ci_envs.py`, …).

The file is intentionally *larger* than before: each field now carries its type, default, and full prose description inline (previously split across a `TYPE_CHECKING` block and a runtime `environment_variables` dict). One declaration site per var is the goal, and it also feeds the docs generator.

## Design decisions

**Docs generated from the model.** `docs/mkdocs/plugins/gen_env_vars.py` walks `Settings.model_fields` at build time and writes `docs/configuration/env_vars.md` (one anchored H3 per env var, grouped by sub-model). Adding or editing a var's `Field(description=...)` updates the docs automatically — no separate edit. `mkdocs.yaml` registers the `gen-files` plugin; `requirements/docs.in` adds `pydantic-settings`.

**Declarative `torch.compile` cache factors.** `compile_factors()` returns the env vars hashed into `torch.compile` cache keys. This was previously *all known vars minus a hand-maintained `ignored_factors` literal* — a second source of truth edited on nearly every merge, which had already drifted (a dead entry with no backing field). It is now a **per-field property**: a var is a compile factor by default, and non-factors carry `json_schema_extra={"compile_factor": False}` on their `Field`. `compile_factors()` derives the exclude-set from the field definitions at runtime, so it cannot drift.

The **opt-out polarity** is deliberate: a forgotten marker leaves a var *in* the factor set (over-hashing → at most a harmless extra cache miss), never silently drops a real factor (which could serve a stale compiled artifact). This is a representation-only change — the set of real compile factors is unchanged apart from dropping the dead entry.

## Behavior changes (all non-breaking)

1. **Bool coercion widened.** Pydantic accepts `yes/no/on/off` in addition to `1/0/true/false` — a superset of the previous accept set.
2. **`VLLM_MM_HASHER_ALGORITHM` and `VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION` are coerced to lower-case.** No-op for `MM_HASHER` (its consumer already `.lower()`s). For `FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION` it's a small fix: `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision()` is case-sensitive and silently no-ops on upper-case input, so `=HIGH` was previously ignored by torch.
3. **`TYPE_CHECKING`-vs-runtime drift fixed.** A few vars had the type-checker view disagreeing with the runtime default (e.g. `VLLM_DP_MASTER_IP` annotated `""` but defaulting to `"127.0.0.1"`). Runtime values are preserved exactly.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_envs.py tests/test_envs_pydantic.py tests/docs/test_env_vars_gen.py` — passing. Covers `VLLM_X` attribute parity, alias/validator/fallback behavior, `compile_factors()` determinism and relocation invariance, the declarative compile-factor drift guard, and the docs-generator output.
- [x] The compile-factor migration was verified exact during development (runtime-derived exclude-set asserted equal to the frozen pre-refactor literal minus the dead entry); that one-time gate was retired for a permanent drift guard.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` (matching CI deps) clean across changed files.
- [x] `mkdocs build` completes; the env-vars page renders one anchored section per var.

To run on CI / Linux + CUDA:

- [ ] Smoke: `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m` starts.
- [ ] `mkdocs build --strict` on readthedocs.

## Local docs build

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-docs
uv pip install --python .venv-docs/bin/python --no-cache-dir -r requirements/docs.txt
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/configuration/env_vars/
```
